newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB aims for China's soft white wheat market.
newsitem.headline: CWB aims for China's soft white wheat market.

text.p: A Canadian Wheat Board market development mission to China last week was a success in raising interest in Canada's soft white wheat, a CWB official said.

"This was more of an information session to provide background so they can consider the quality we have and fit it with their needs and having discussions about the quality characteristics they're looking for. I'd say the program was a success," CWB Market Development Director Gordon Bacon said.
The CWB supplies about 50 percent of China's wheat import needs, mostly in hard red spring wheats, Bacon said.
Australia is China's chief supplier of soft white wheats followed by, to a smaller degree, the United States, he said.
"We talked about its potential applications in a range of products including noodles but also cakes, sweet goods and steam buns," Bacon said.
Protein content of Canadian soft white wheat averages around 10.5 percent. Bread wheats like hard red spring have higher protein contents.
"It's application isn't limited to one particular product but obviously, by its nature, is most suited to confectionary goods," Bacon said.
The trade mission met with soft white wheat users in Beijing and Guangzhou and barley maltsters and beer brewers in Dalian and Quingdao, he said.
